text:
Aisha: Heads-up — our telemetry picked up a spike of TLS handshake errors from eu-west and ap-south around 11:05 UTC. Looks correlated with yesterday's RBAC prune for keystore roles. Logs attached below.
Tom: on it. Can you paste the exact error line? :eyes:
Aisha: sure — excerpt:
```
2026-03-21T11:05:12Z INFO proxy TLS handshake failed: client_hello parse error: unknown key-id 'ephemeral-keystore-045f' source=service-a eu-west-1
```
Aisha: notice the key-id is an ephemeral keystore entry that should have been rotated/removed by the rotator job.
Raj: what did the RBAC prune remove? any keystore roles touched? I thought we only removed unused iam:Decrypt for svc-legacy.
Aisha: the change list from yesterday: removed role "keystore-operator-legacy" and tightened "keystore-reader" to deny unwrap for a few service principals. I suspect the rotator couldn't unwrap some keys after that.
Emily: @Raj fyi — rotator logs show repeated KMS::AccessDenied for the same key-id starting at 10:58 UTC. That lines up.
certbot: Rotator job output (filtered):
```
rotator-2026-03-21T10:58Z ERROR unwrap failed key=ephemeral-keystore-045f err=AccessDenied
rotator-2026-03-21T10:59Z WARN fallback: keeping old cert until manual intervention
```
Tom: If rotator couldn't unwrap, some proxies kept serving the stale cert entry until eviction. The proxies then hit peer services that had already dropped permission to accept that key-id, causing handshake parse errors.
Aisha: question: did the RBAC change also remove any IAM condition on region tag? Could explain why eu-west & ap-south only.
Raj: yes — we added a condition restricting keystore unwrap to region:us-east-1 for that role. Bad timing, my bad. :grimacing:
Emily: ok, mitigation options:
- rollback the RBAC change for keystore-operator-legacy (quick)
- grant rotator the explicit kms:Decrypt on affected keys (targeted)
- force rotator rerun with --force-unwrap (risky)
Which should we do for fastest RTO?
Tom: rollback + targeted grant sounds safest. Rollback first so rotator can finish unwrapping without forcing.
Aisha: agreed. I'm going to patch the IAM change now and watch rotator logs.
oncall-bot: Incident created: SEC-2026-03-21-004 — "Ephemeral keystore unwrap failures causing TLS handshake errors". Owners: Aisha, Tom. SLA: P0.
Aisha: RBAC rollback applied at 11:12 UTC. Rotator now shows progress:
```
rotator-2026-03-21T11:13Z INFO unwrap succeeded key=ephemeral-keystore-045f
rotator-2026-03-21T11:14Z INFO rotation complete for service-a proxy
```
Tom: I've restarted the edge proxies in eu-west and ap-south to clear cached cert references.
Emily: Observability note — add an alert for repeated KMS::AccessDenied for rotator (threshold >3 in 5m) and correlate with proxy handshake failures.
Raj: I'll open a follow-up to tighten the RBAC change so it doesn't accidentally restrict the rotator. Maybe a managed policy with explicit allow for rotator principal.
Aisha: Postmortem action items:
- (A) Add integration test that simulates RBAC prune against rotator and fails CI if unwrap breaks.
- (B) Improve rotator telemetry: emit key-id + principal + error in structured audit logs.
- (C) Add our new alert that Emily mentioned.
- (D) Document region-scoped IAM conditions impact on keystore unwraps.
Tom: also add a small runbook snippet:
```
If KMS::AccessDenied seen by rotator:
1) check recent IAM changes (gitops)
2) temporarily restore previous role
3) let rotator finish unwrap + rotation
4) audit keys and narrow permissions safely
```
Aisha: going to mark incident as mitigated after 11:20 UTC once alert rates stabilize. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
Raj: sorry for the break, will follow up with PR for rotator allowlist.
Emily: adding the alert + runbook to the security playbooks repo now.
certbot: reminder: scheduled global ephemeral-keystore GC tomorrow 03:00 UTC — ensure rotator has perms across regions before then.
Aisha: noted. Closing thread once postmortem doc is up."
